Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset: one reusable landscape ground layer for graphic design, with actual PNG alpha transparency.
Input image 1 is the ONLY style reference: derive the material, colors, texture, visual medium AND characteristic geometry from it. Design an original landscape composition; do not copy the pictured object, any letters or symbols, or previous generic dune arrangements.
Framing principle: WIDE landscape canvas, 3:2. The landscape sits in the LOWER portion of the frame and continues off the bottom and both side edges. Fill the full bottom edge with foreground terrain. Its irregular upper silhouette is mostly around 40–55% down the frame, with some peaks reaching about 30% down. Leave substantial empty transparent space above. See the ground from a low oblique viewpoint, close enough to show texture and with visible upper surfaces where separate design elements can later be placed. No visible front edge or floating island pedestal. Compose asymmetrically with a readable foreground, middle ground and upper contour; keep some generous usable surface areas.
Critical: The shape of the terrain and its upper silhouette must express THIS reference material, not merely recolor smooth generic hills. Adapt the terrain structure as specified below. A connected landscape fills the foreground.
Render in the reference's style with high-quality tactile detail, coherent directional light and clear depth. Everything outside the terrain is fully transparent, with no sky, background plane, fog, halo, bloom or cast shadow outside it. No products, characters, trees, buildings, text, logos, watermarks or decorative unrelated objects. Do not simulate transparency with a grid or a black/white background.

Material-specific geometry and style:
Smoky clear quartz, subtly lavender-gray with silvery prismatic faces, internal striations and fractures as in the reference. Create an interlocking bed of crystalline slabs and angular terraces that rises into irregular clusters of quartz points. Sharp straight planar facets, broken diagonals and chisel-like crystal terminations; the skyline MUST be jagged and angular. Vary the size and direction of prisms. Keep a broad faceted shelf in the foreground for placement. No rounded dunes or smooth liquid blobs. The terrain itself is crystalline, not ordinary ground with crystals scattered on top.
